question.en: The expenditure of Sudha is 150% more than her savings. If her expenditure decreases by 3% and savings increase by 21.5%, then by what percent does her income increase?

solution.approach: Official Answer: Option B (**4%**).

trapAlert.en: "150% more than savings" means Expenditure = 100 + 150 = 250 (NOT 150!) when Savings = 100.
trapAlert.hi: "बचत से 150% अधिक" का अर्थ व्यय $= 100 + 150 = 250$ है (न कि 150!) — यह परीक्षा का सबसे बड़ा जाल है।

steps.en:
1) Let Savings $S = 100 \Rightarrow$ Expenditure $E = 100 + 150 = 250 \Rightarrow$ Income $I = 350$.
2) Change in $E = -3\%$ of $250 = -7.5$; Change in $S = +21.5\%$ of $100 = +21.5$.
3) Net change in Income $= 14$ on $350 \Rightarrow \frac{14}{350} \times 100 = \mathbf{4\%}$.
steps.hi:
1) मानें बचत $S = 100 \Rightarrow$ व्यय $E = 250$ तथा आय $I = 350$।
2) व्यय में परिवर्तन $= -3\%$ of $250 = -7.5$; बचत में परिवर्तन $= +21.5$।
3) आय में निवल वृद्धि $= 14$ पर कुल $350 \Rightarrow \frac{14}{350} \times 100 = \mathbf{4\%}$।

solution.en:
Method 1: Base-100 Assumption: 1) Let Savings $S = 100 \Rightarrow$ Expenditure $E = 100 + 150 = 250 \Rightarrow$ Income $I = 350$.
2) Change in $E = -3\%$ of $250 = -7.5$; Change in $S = +21.5\%$ of $100 = +21.5$.
3) Net change in Income $= 14$ on $350 \Rightarrow \frac{14}{350} \times 100 = \mathbf{4\%}$.

Method 2: Weighted Average Ratio Trick: Ratio $E : S = 250 : 100 = 5 : 2$ (Total $= 7$ parts).
